title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: SkillsFuture review and consolidation
sections.summary: The speaker says 2025 marks 10 years of SkillsFuture and calls for a comprehensive review to align it with workforce needs and streamline efforts across agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The year 2025 marks 10 years since the Government launched the national SkillsFuture movement with the aim of promoting CET as a national priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I submit that it is now timely to conduct a comprehensive review of SkillsFuture to ensure alignment with evolving workforce needs, as well as consolidate efforts and streamline offerings across different arms, such as Employment and Employability Institute (e2i), Workforce Singapore (WSG), SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), training providers and the various Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) in Singapore, including the various Ministries and sector agencies and associations.

sections.label: Employment of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The passage states more can be done to shift mindsets and reach the Enabling Masterplan 2030 target of 40% employment for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While great strides have been made through initiatives like the Open Door Programme and the Enabling Employment Credit, more can be done to shift mindsets and reach the Enabling Masterplan 2030 target of 40% employment rate for persons with disabilities by 2030.

sections.label: DSA review and lower-income students
sections.summary: The passage notes full Subject-Based Banding implementation and an MOE review of DSA, urging consideration and support for lower-income students and transparent selection criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Last year, we fully implemented Subject-Based Banding, replacing the old system of streaming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am also glad to hear that MOE will review the Direct School Admission (DSA) system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As we embark on this review, I submit that greater consideration should be given to students from lower-income families, who have less access to enrichment classes and private coaching or even exposure to high-cost non-academic talents in sports or the arts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Besides expanding the selection process to account for potential in addition to performance, the Ministry can consider offering additional resources and financial support to students from lower-income families to discover and hone their non-academic talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Schools should also be required to publish clear and transparent selection criteria and rubrics, as well as conflict-of-interest policies.

sections.label: Barriers to broader success vision
sections.summary: The passage states that Minister Chan Chun Sing championed a broader definition of success and lifelong learning, but three significant barriers could hinder this vision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Minister Chan Chun Sing himself has painstakingly championed a broader definition of success and lifelong learning, but three significant barriers could hinder this vision.

sections.label: Plans for mindset shift
sections.summary: The passage asks what additional plans exist to foster a mindset shift, noting Minister Chan Chun Sing said systemic changes alone are insufficient without cultural shifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Minister Chan Chun Sing himself has rightly pointed out that systemic changes alone are not sufficient without cultural shifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But since MOE has done as much as it deems possible, systemically, what additional plans are there in place to foster a mindset shift?

sections.label: SEN students in mainstream schools
sections.summary: The passage states that over 80% of students with mild to moderate SEN are in mainstream schools, necessitating robust support systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Over 80% of our students with mild to moderate SEN are in mainstream schools, necessitating robust support systems.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and disability support
sections.summary: Adult learners with disabilities need lifelong learning, but the cliff effect after age 18 stops their progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Their need for lifelong learning is critical as technology transforms our world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, the "cliff effect" – where support drops drastically after age 18 – stops progress for many of the adult learners with disabilities.

sections.label: Private education business declaration
sections.summary: The speaker declares being in the private education business.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, first, let me declare that I am in the private education business.

sections.label: Class sizes versus OECD average
sections.summary: In 2023 average class sizes were 33.6 in primary and 32.6 in secondary schools, above the OECD average of 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As of 2023, the average class size was 33.6 in primary schools and 32.6 in secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is far higher than the average public primary school class in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries, which is 21.

sections.label: Educator support and lifelong learning
sections.summary: The speaker urges making PSLE optional, reducing class sizes, and asks how the Ministry supports educators' learning, well-being and mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Once again, I urge the Minister to consider making PSLE optional by implementing a pilot through-train programme and to reduce class sizes for the benefit of our dwindling number of children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Providing continuous learning opportunities to educators, including collaboration across borders, as well as robust systems to support mental health and work-life balance, will assist educators remain confident and competent in the global environment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, how is the Ministry supporting educators to adapt to rapidly changing global needs and adequately prepare them for future challenges in the education sector?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In what ways is the Ministry facilitating the creation of an environment that fosters and promotes the importance of lifelong learning among educators, and what strategies are being implemented to guide educators towards learning and teaching driven by curiosity and passion?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What initiatives are being introduced to ensure the curriculum for educators remains relevant and forward-thinking, and supports their continuous professional growth?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And finally, what measures are being taken to support the mental health and well-being of educators?

sections.label: L1R5 to L1R4 aggregate score change
sections.summary: The L1R5 aggregate score system moved in 1980 to L1R4, reducing relevant subjects from five to four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the 1970s, the L1R5 system, or the calculation of a student's aggregate score was based on their best language subject (L1) and five relevant academic subjects (R5).

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This system moved in 1980 to the L1R4 system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of relevant subjects for which the aggregate score was counted was reduced from five to four.

sections.label: Junior colleges moving to new buildings
sections.summary: As of November 2024, three junior colleges are slated to move into new buildings by January 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of November 2024, I believe that three JCs, Temasek Junior College, ASRJC and JPJC have been slated to move into new buildings by January 2028.

sections.label: SEN education support and funding
sections.summary: The SEN Masterplan and Inclusive Education framework aim to integrate children with SEN into mainstream schools, with funding for SPED facilities and SEN support in polytechnics and ITEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The SEN Masterplan, our national framework, aims to enhance the quality and accessibility of SEN education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Masterplan for Inclusive Education was introduced to ensure that children with SEN are integrated into mainstream schools wherever possible and that schools provide appropriate support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Funding for SPED schools to create better facilities, resources and teaching staff to support SEN students is a plus, so schools can hire specialised staff and invest in assistive and supportive technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There is also mainstreaming of SEN support and services in polytechnics and the ITEs.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training participation decline
sections.summary: SkillsFuture has been enhanced over the years, but training participation rate fell to 40.7% in 2024, the lowest in nine years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Over the years, SkillsFuture has been enhanced to encourage adoption and advance workforce impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, despite the strong efforts, training participation rate declined to 40.7% in 2024, the lowest in nine years.

sections.label: Tiered accreditation for CET providers
sections.summary: Singapore should establish a tiered accreditation system for CET providers based on industry endorsement, programme quality and workforce outcomes, with government funding tied to accreditation level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This one-size-fits-all approach weakens SkillsFuture's strategic effectiveness as a workforce development tool and risks diluting its impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, Madam, to address this, Singapore should establish a tiered accreditation system that categorises CET providers based on industry endorsement, their programme quality and workforce outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Government funding should be directly tied to their level of accreditation, ensuring that providers with higher quality standards receive higher levels of support.

sections.label: CET-integrated degree programme pilot
sections.summary: A pilot of CET-integrated degree programmes for in-employment diploma holders in advanced manufacturing was recently announced in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Singapore, I am encouraged with the recently announced pilot of CET-integrated degree programmes for in-employment diploma holders in advanced manufacturing.

sections.label: Absolute entry criteria for universities
sections.summary: One strategy is to alter entry criteria for autonomous universities like SUSS, SIT and SUTD so they admit students meeting absolute entry criteria rather than relative to all applicants.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One strategy we can consider is to alter the criteria for entry into certain autonomous universities, such as the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), such that they can take in students so long as they meet absolute entry criteria, rather than relative to all applicants for a particular programme.

sections.label: STEM and California university admissions
sections.summary: In STEM subjects this could be as high as nine out of 10 students, and California State University admission is more liberal, with assured entry for some low-income first-generation students.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And in the science, engineering, technology and mathematics (STEM) subjects, this could be as high as nine out of 10 students.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And while the prestigious University of California system only guarantees a spot to high school graduates that fall within the top 9% of the state's high school cohort, admission into the next tier, what is known as the California State University system, is actually much more liberal and low-income residents who are first-generation, under-represented college students may even be assured entry into certain majors, subject to a commitment by the student that they complete their studies within four years.

sections.label: Expanding university access and graduate supply
sections.summary: The passage argues that entry requirements should let qualifying students complete study, that Singaporeans qualifying for local universities should have degree opportunities, and that graduate oversupply concerns are offset by shortages of skilled tech professionals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Those should be chosen to ensure that any student that meets the minimum requirements should be able to successfully complete the course of study.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And perhaps, more importantly, if you believe, as I do, that any Singaporean who qualifies for a local university should have the opportunity to pursue a degree, then we should not shy away from expanding the system and set aside the resources necessary to ensure that this is so.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The third concern is that this liberal approach may end up churning out too many graduates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But in reality, there is a shortage of certain skilled professionals, especially in tech, and companies often rate skills over degrees.

sections.label: Looser entry, tighter graduation conditions
sections.summary: The passage states that loosening entry criteria while tightening graduation conditions keeps tertiary offerings nimble, and that flexible entry has not undermined top French, German and Californian universities, with the suggestion limited to the applied tier of AUs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Loosening the criteria for entry, while simultaneously tightening the conditions for graduation will help keep our tertiary offerings nimble, since we need to worry less about how failing out already small intakes could pre-emptively decimate programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One may finally argue that removing the competitive entry could weaken the quality of our lauded universities, such as the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As suggested earlier, more flexible entry requirements do not appear to have undermined the standing of the best French, German and Californian universities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In any case, the suggestion is limited to the applied tier of our AUs, those that were less oriented toward academic accomplishment and research output to begin with.

sections.label: Polytechnic common entry programmes expansion
sections.summary: The passage states that polytechnic common entry programmes have expanded significantly, letting students explore fields before specialising, with one in four polytechnic students now entering them, and asks MOE to share insights on benefits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The polytechnic common entry programmes (CEPs) have expanded significantly, allowing students to explore different fields before selecting a specialisation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With one in four polytechnic students now entering to the CEPs, could MOE share insights on how they have benefitted?

sections.label: Republic Polytechnic broad-based diplomas AY2025
sections.summary: The passage states that Republic Polytechnic will begin offering broad-based diploma options in Academic Year 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Republic Polytechnic will begin offering broad-based diploma options in Academic Year 2025 (AY2025).

sections.label: Increase in SEN officers
sections.summary: The passage states that according to MOE, the number of SEN officers in mainstream schools increased from around 450 in 2017 to about 680 as of July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to MOE, "the number of SEN officers in mainstream schools has increased from around 450 in 2017 to about 680 as of July 2024".

sections.label: More recreational sports CCAs
sections.summary: The passage states that schools should open up more recreational sports CCAs for popular sports to cater to students who want to play sports for leisure but lack formal training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To cater to students who want to play sports for leisure but lack formal training, schools should open up more recreational sports CCAs for popular sports.

sections.label: Excusing student athletes from school training
sections.summary: High performance sports training usually occurs outside school, so student athletes should have the option to be excused from school training and competition to focus on becoming world-class athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: High performance sports training usually takes place outside of school, at training programmes run by National Sports Associations or private academies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These student athletes should have the option to be excused from school training and competition so as to be able to better focus on becoming world-class athletes who can compete on the world stage and win medals for Singapore.

sections.label: GeBIZ for coaching services procurement
sections.summary: Instructors without contracts are left without work until the next bidding cycle, so whether GeBIZ is the most suitable procurement process for coaching services needs assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, instructors who do not secure any contracts are left without work until the next bidding cycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We need to assess whether GeBIZ is the most suitable procurement process for coaching services.

sections.label: Students learning CPF, loans, taxes, insurance
sections.summary: Students should not leave school without understanding the Central Provident Fund, housing loans, taxes and insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: Students should not leave school without understanding the Central Provident Fund (CPF), housing loans, taxes and insurance.

sections.label: IMH study on youth social media use
sections.summary: An Institute of Mental Health study in Singapore found youths spending more than three hours daily on social media are more likely to experience depression, anxiety and stress symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Singapore, a study by the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) found that youths who spend more time – more than three hours daily – on social media are more likely to experience symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress.

sections.label: Private tuition industry value
sections.summary: Private tuition is now a $1.8 billion industry in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Private tuition is now a $1.8 billion industry in Singapore.

sections.label: Revamping PSLE and O level assessment
sections.summary: Quoting Minister Chan Chun Sing on discerning truth, quality and relevance, the speaker recommends MOE revamp PSLE and O level assessment models toward classroom participation, portfolios, project work and discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I quote Minister Chan Chun Sing's recent speech at an Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) lecture, "Beyond just being able to distil information, learning to discern truth, quality and relevance has become more critical." How can we evolve our assessment models to capture this new emphasis?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I recommend that MOE revamp the assessment models for the PSLE and "O" levels and shift to a higher proportion of classroom participation, portfolio building, project work, discussions and less on-paper examinations.

sections.label: AI in student assessment
sections.summary: AI can help revamp student assessment to capture qualities like engagement, originality, vocabulary progress, creativity and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: AI can play a role in helping us revamp the way we assess students to capture qualities like engagement level, originality of thought, progress in personal vocabulary and articulation, creativity, confidence and other observations.

sections.label: Parenting for Wellness Initiative
sections.summary: The PfW Initiative equips parents with tools and strategies, and the passage asks how the toolbox is distributed and its effectiveness measured.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: In today's digital age, where young people face increasing stress and online risks, the Parenting for Wellness (PfW) Initiative is a timely effort to equip parents with practical tools and strategies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Could MOE share how the PfW Toolbox for Parents is distributed and how its effectiveness is measured?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: How will MOE ensure that schools have sufficient support systems and trained personnel to assess mental health risks and intervene effectively?

sections.label: Embracing diversity of talents
sections.summary: It states that diversity of talents must be recognised, respected and embraced to enable Singaporeans to thrive amid uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, we must recognise, respect and embrace a diversity of talents to enable Singaporeans to thrive even amidst the uncertainties and untidiness of the world.

sections.label: SEN students in schools
sections.summary: About 30,000 SEN students, four in five, attend mainstream schools, while 8,500 with moderate to severe SEN receive support in SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, about 30,000 SEN students, or four in five, attend our mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The remaining 8,500 – with moderate to severe SEN – receive special support in our SPED schools.

sections.label: TRANSIT implementation in primary schools
sections.summary: As of January 2025, TRANSIT has been implemented in 98% of primary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As of January 2025, we have implemented TRANSIT in 98% of primary schools.

sections.label: Growth in SEN officers
sections.summary: The number of SEN officers grew from 450 in 2016 to nearly 750 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Beyond teachers, we have grown our number of SEN officers from 450 in 2016 to nearly 750 in 2024.

sections.label: Digital solutions for SPED schools
sections.summary: MOE is working with SPED schools and SSAs to explore digital solutions for SPED school processes, including extending existing MOE systems.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: So, for example, while teachers in mainstream schools can leverage technologies to track their students' progress and learning outcomes, some educators in our SPED schools do so manually today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are working with SPED schools and our SSAs to explore possible digital solutions for SPED school processes, including the potential extension of existing MOE systems to our SPED schools.

sections.label: SPED communities of practice
sections.summary: A SPED COP for Multiple Disabilities was established last October, and a SPED COP for Autism will be underway in the second half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The platform will support SPED educators in keeping up with new practices in the sector and across the many sub-specialisations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We established the inaugural SPED COP for Multiple Disabilities last October, led by Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore, with members from Rainbow Centre and Asian Women's Welfare Association (AWWA).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Another SPED COP for Autism will be underway in the second half of 2025.

sections.label: ITE internship support for SEN
sections.summary: ITE will expand internship support so more students with SEN can benefit from structured job support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ITE will expand the internship support provided so that more students with SEN can benefit from such structured job support.

sections.label: Enhanced three-year ITE curricular structure
sections.summary: Starting with selected courses from AY2022, ITE introduced an enhanced three-year curricular structure leading directly to a Higher Nitec certification.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Starting with selected courses from AY2022, ITE introduced a new enhanced three-year curricular structure leading directly to a Higher Nitec certification.

sections.label: ITE Progression Award extension
sections.summary: The IPA provides $15,000 to young ITE graduates, with about $90 million awarded to about 12,000 graduates, and will extend to WSQ diplomas from 1 June.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last year, we introduced the ITE Progression Award (IPA), which provides young ITE graduates with a total of $15,000 to upskill to a diploma earlier in their careers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We recognise that many ITE graduates aspire to upgrade their qualifications with higher level skills and can benefit from financial support to defray education costs and boost their savings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that by end March, we would have awarded around $90 million to support the upgrading journeys of about 12,000 ITE graduates who enrolled in or completed their diplomas in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To support our ITE graduates' different upskilling needs, we will extend the IPA to those who are upskilling via diplomas offered under the Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) from 1 June this year.

sections.label: Support for SEN and ITE pathways
sections.summary: Support for SEN students and families will be strengthened, Higher Malay Language eligibility revised, and the IPA extended to WSQ diploma courses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will strengthen our support for students with SEN and their families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will work closely with the social services agencies and other agencies to enhance curriculum support for students as well as strengthen professional development for educators in SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With the revised eligibility criteria for Higher Mother Tongue Language in secondary schools, students who excel in Malay Language can take Higher Malay Language, regardless of their overall academic performance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will continue to provide specialised programmes to strengthen our students’ proficiency of the Malay Language, to develop future stewards of Malay language and culture.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will also provide multiple pathways to meet the diverse aspirations of our students, and look forward to more students benefiting from the transition of all ITE courses to the newly enhanced three-year ITE curricular structure by Academic Year 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To provide opportunities for more ITE graduates to upskill via a diploma, we will extend the IPA to diploma courses offered under the Singapore WSQ.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Queen Bees appointed
sections.summary: SSG has appointed 37 SkillsFuture Queen Bees in 14 sectors, benefiting 5,300 companies in these sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Today, SSG has appointed 37 SkillsFuture Queen Bees in 14 sectors, benefiting 5,300 companies in these sectors.

sections.label: Employer training participation and subsidies
sections.summary: Employer participation in SSG-supported training doubled from around 12,000 in 2018 to over 24,000 in 2024, mostly SMEs, with about $440 million disbursed annually in course fee subsidies over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The number of employers participating in training supported by SSG has doubled from around 12,000 in 2018 to more than 24,000 in 2024 and the majority are SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In the last three years, SSG disbursed about $440 million annually in course fee subsidies.

sections.label: Support for training and workforce costs
sections.summary: Support includes jobs and skills insights, online resources, course fee subsidies up to 90% for SMEs, a new $10,000 SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit from second half of 2026, and enhanced corporate tax deduction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: For example, by providing jobs and skills insights, online resources and tools as well as substantial support to defray training and other workforce development costs such as generous SSG's course fee subsidies at up to 90% for SMEs, a fresh $10,000 SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit from second half of 2026, which will be enhanced to allow out-of-pocket costs to be offset upfront and corporate tax deduction for eligible training that has been enhanced from 100% to 400%, up to $400,000 per year, under the Enterprise Innovation Scheme.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit Mid-Career top-up uptake
sections.summary: Since the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up launched in May 2024, more than 28,000 Singaporeans have tapped on it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Since launching the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of $4,000 in May 2024, I am heartened to see that more than 28,000 Singaporeans have tapped on the $4,000 top-up.

sections.label: Mid-Career Training Allowance applications
sections.summary: From next Monday, mid-career Singaporeans pursuing full-time training can apply for the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance, sized at 50% of average salary over the latest 12-month period, with payouts from $300 to $3,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: From next Monday onwards, mid-career Singaporeans who pursue full-time training like Mr Song can apply for the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The training allowance is sized at 50% of their average salary over the latest 12-month period and the payout will range from $300 to $3,000 per month.

sections.label: Maximum training allowance duration
sections.summary: Individuals can receive training allowance for a maximum of 24 months, regardless of full-time or part-time training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)

sections.summary: The passage states Singapore has a porous and continuous meritocracy, with reduced examination load, L1R5 to L1R4 changes, and Full SBB grouping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why we have gone on a porous and continuous meritocracy, where everyone can pivot and pursue different options as they progress in life without being defined by the stakes of one high-stake examination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why we are reducing examination load with "Learn More, Test Less".

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing

sentences.text: This is also why we group students according to their abilities and interest in different domains at different stages of their learning journey, like Full SBB, so that we do not teach to a child's average ability or a class' average abilities.
